title: Macrophage Polarization and Cytokine Networks in Solid Tumors
text: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt an M2-like phenotype that suppresses anti-tumor immunity. We profiled the cytokine milieu of solid tumors and found that IL-10, TGF-beta, and IL-6 dominate the immunosuppressive landscape. Reprogramming macrophages toward an M1 phenotype restored immune response and slowed tumor growth. These observations are consistent with the emerging consensus that macrophage polarization is a key determinant of outcomes in the tumor microenvironment. The role of metabolic reprogramming in macrophage polarization remains unclear and needs investigation.
